question: Will a U.S. federal agency announce new or expanded model evaluation agreements with both OpenAI and Anthropic before September 3, 2026?

factors.description: Documented non-publication posture on exactly this program. Fortune (Aug 4, 2026): 'White House won't publicly release AI model evaluation framework it reviewed today with Meta, Nvidia, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic' — details 'kept under wraps, only known to a select group of companies that may choose to participate.' Axios (Aug 4): 'White House plans to keep AI framework under wraps'; benchmarks/thresholds classified. WSJ: days after EO 14409 the administration directed CAISI to stop issuing public reports of its model assessments. The Aug 1 EO deadline lapsed with zero public deliverables (no Federal Register notices, no NIST/CISA publications, no OSTP statements). Downweighted from my initial read because CAISI kept publishing partnership-type items (July 2026 Kimi K3 joint assessment, OpenMined CRADA, GSA MOU) — the curb targeted model assessments, not all announcements.

Elevated activity environment: EO 14409 (June 2, 2026) mandated a voluntary pre-release review framework; it was finalized around the Aug 1 deadline and ~a dozen labs were briefed at a White House 'close the loop' meeting on Aug 4. The program is entering implementation/enrollment, and every participating lab must paper its participation under a new instrument — mechanically raising the hazard of a qualifying announcement versus a quiet baseline.

Wrong expansion vector. Per a White House official, the framework 'currently applies only to closed models from Anthropic and OpenAI,' and the advertised next expansion is toward open-weight models (Meta, Nvidia) once they reach frontier level. The May 5, 2026 CAISI release is a counter-precedent rather than a supporting one: it officially named Google DeepMind, Microsoft and xAI, while the OpenAI/Anthropic renegotiations surfaced only through Bloomberg reporting, never an official release naming them. That is precisely this question's failure mode — real activity, no official announcement covering both.

Revealed preference at the natural announcement moment, plus elapsed time. The Aug 3-4 framework finalization and lab briefing — the single most likely trigger for an agreements announcement — produced no public agency announcement, and falls before the Aug 10 window start so cannot resolve the question (the window appears drawn deliberately to exclude it). 9 of the 24 window days (Aug 10-19) have elapsed with nothing qualifying found across many query formulations.

Degraded CAISI institutional capacity: director Chris Fall resigned July 20, 2026 after ~3 months; NIST Director Arvind Raman is dual-hatted as acting head while a permanent successor is sought; Rep. Khanna has publicly flagged the vacuum. Leaderless agencies issue fewer flagship announcements, and late August is a DC recess lull.

Countervailing pressure toward disclosure: Senate Democrats' letter calls the strategy 'ad-hoc and unpredictable' and demands an unclassified response on model-access policy; The Hill reports the closed-door framework blindsided the policy sector. Announcing that agreements exist (while keeping contents classified) is a cheap, direct rebuttal, and both labs publicly lobbied for the 30-day review and would welcome credit.

Lenient-resolution pathway: NIST previously posted a non-press-release page ('CAISI Works with OpenAI and Anthropic to Promote Secure AI Innovation', ~Aug 2025) describing joint security evaluation work with both labs alongside UK AISI. A similar post, or agency confirmation accompanying paired company blog posts, could be read as a 'materially expanded' evaluation domain. This is the single largest YES contributor in my Monte Carlo.

Verification weakness (widens uncertainty, mild net negative given status-quo default). Primary sources were largely unreadable: nist.gov/caisi and the NIST news search returned JS-rendered shells, the August 2026 news index 404'd, and no date-filtered news search was available. My 'nothing found in Aug 10-19' rests on generic web search, so absence of evidence is weaker here than usual — though six independent query angles all returned the same May and early-August items.

summary:
Resolves YES only if a U.S. federal AGENCY OFFICIALLY ANNOUNCES, strictly between Aug 10 and Sept 3 2026, new or materially expanded voluntary agreements to evaluate frontier models from BOTH OpenAI and Anthropic. Status quo is NO.

The decisive structural fact is that the biggest relevant event sits just outside the window. EO 14409 (June 2, 2026) mandated a voluntary pre-release review framework; it was finalized around the Aug 1 deadline and the White House convened ~a dozen labs — including OpenAI and Anthropic — on Aug 4 to "close the loop." That was the natural announcement moment, it occurred before Aug 10, and it produced no public agency announcement. Instead, Fortune and Axios reported on Aug 4 that the White House has no plans to publicly release the framework; participation details stay "under wraps, only known to a select group of companies." WSJ reported CAISI was directed to stop publishing model assessments. The Aug 1 statutory deliverables lapsed with zero public output. CAISI has had no permanent director since July 20 (NIST's Arvind Raman is dual-hatted as acting head).

I checked the pre-publication trap explicitly: the window start (Aug 10) precedes published_at (Aug 15), so this is Case 1 and an Aug 10-15 event would legitimately count — I searched for one and found nothing.

The strongest counter-precedent is the one the question's own background cites. On May 5, 2026 CAISI did issue a formal agreements release — but it named Google DeepMind, Microsoft and xAI, while the OpenAI/Anthropic renegotiations surfaced only via Bloomberg, never an official release naming them. That is exactly this question's failure mode: real activity, no qualifying official announcement. Compounding it, a White House official says the framework already covers OpenAI's and Anthropic's closed models, with the advertised next expansion aimed at open-weight developers — so the modal next announcement adds different companies.

Quantitatively I decomposed rather than argued narratively: P(any genre announcement in the 24-day window) × P(covers both | announcement) × P(clears the "materially expanded" fine print), plus an additive lenient-resolution allowance for a NIST informational post like the ~Aug 2025 "CAISI Works with OpenAI and Anthropic" page. Monte Carlo center ≈ 4.5%; sensitivity across secrecy multiplier 0.25-0.60, activity multiplier 1.8-3.0, p_both 0.25-0.45 and leniency 0.02-0.08 gives 2.5-6.9% — stable, not knife-edge. Anchor (−2.94) plus factor sum (−0.53) implies ≈3%.

I settle at 6%, above both the factor sum and the simulation center, conceding the premortem's two strongest points: CAISI kept issuing partnership-type announcements (July 2026 Kimi K3 assessment, OpenMined CRADA, GSA MOU) even while assessment reporting was curbed, so the secrecy read was over-broad; and EO 14409 creates genuinely new paperwork that would qualify as a previously-not-covered access arrangement. The main known weakness is that government press pages rendered as empty shells and no date-filtered news search was available, so my "nothing in Aug 10-19" is softer evidence than I would like.
reasoning:
**Forecast: 6% (NO)**

## Reasoning

**What must happen:** A U.S. federal *agency* must *officially announce*, strictly between Aug 10 and Sept 3, 2026, new or materially expanded voluntary agreements to evaluate frontier models from **both** OpenAI and Anthropic.

**The decisive finding:** The biggest relevant event falls just *outside* the window. EO 14409 (June 2, 2026) mandated a voluntary pre-release review framework; it was finalized around its Aug 1 deadline, and the White House convened ~a dozen labs — including OpenAI and Anthropic — on **Aug 4** to "close the loop." That was the natural announcement moment, it preceded Aug 10, and it produced no public agency announcement. Instead:

- Fortune and Axios (Aug 4): the White House has **no plans to publicly release** the framework — details stay "under wraps, only known to a select group of companies"
- WSJ: CAISI was directed to **stop publishing** model assessments
- The Aug 1 EO deliverables lapsed with zero public output (no Federal Register notices, no NIST/CISA publications)
- CAISI has had **no permanent director** since July 20; NIST's Arvind Raman is dual-hatted as acting head

**The strongest counter-precedent is the question's own background.** On May 5, 2026 CAISI *did* issue a formal agreements release — but it named Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI. The OpenAI/Anthropic renegotiations surfaced only via Bloomberg, never an official release naming them. That is precisely this question's failure mode: real activity, no qualifying official announcement. A White House official also states the framework *already* covers both labs' closed models, with the next expansion aimed at open-weight developers — so the modal next announcement adds different companies.

**Method:** I decomposed rather than argued narratively — P(any genre announcement) × P(covers both) × P(clears the "materially expanded" fine print), plus an allowance for lenient resolution via a NIST informational post like the ~Aug 2025 "CAISI Works with OpenAI and Anthropic" page. Monte Carlo center ≈4.5%; sensitivity across four parameters gives 2.5–6.9%, so the estimate is stable rather than knife-edge.

I landed at 6% — above both my factor sum (~3%) and simulation center — conceding two points from my own premortem: CAISI *did* keep issuing partnership-type announcements (July's Kimi K3 assessment, an OpenMined CRADA, a GSA MOU) even while assessment reporting was curbed, so my secrecy read was over-broad; and EO 14409 creates genuinely new paperwork that would qualify as a previously-uncovered access arrangement.

**Two caveats worth stating plainly.** First, I verified the Aug 10–19 stretch only through generic web search — `nist.gov/caisi` and the NIST news search returned JavaScript shells, the August 2026 news index 404'd, and no date-filtered news tool was available. Six query angles all returned the same May and early-August items, but a GovDelivery bulletin from mid-August could plausibly have escaped me.
